messages.content: 去年現代藝術博物館的會員們有多頻繁地參觀？

function.name: most_frequent_visitor
function.description: Retrieve the visitor who visited the museum the most within a given period. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

start_date.description: The start date of the period, format: yyyy-mm-dd.

end_date.description: The end date of the period, format: yyyy-mm-dd.

minimum_visits.description: The minimum number of visits to qualify. Default: 1

message.reasoning:
The user asks (in Chinese) "How frequently did members visit last year at the contemporary art museum?" They want data about frequency of visits among members. We have a tool `most_frequent_visitor` which retrieves the visitor with most visits within a period. But they ask about overall frequency? Maybe we can use this function to get the top frequent visitor and then compute average or something.

But maybe there's another function not listed; but only one available. So we need to call it. Provide arguments: museum_name: "Contemporary Art Museum" presumably. Start date: 2025-01-01? Wait it's last year relative to current date 2026-05-18. Last year would be 2025? Actually if today is May 18, 2026, last year refers to 2025 calendar year. So start_date=2025-01-01, end_date=2025-12-31. Minimum_visits default 1.

We might also interpret "members" as all visitors flagged as member. But our function doesn't filter membership status. It just returns the most frequent visitor. That may suffice.

Thus we will call the function. Then respond accordingly. Let's do so.
